prompt: Omar takes on five new goals at once — language, running, coding, saving, and a side project — and after a month none has moved. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: He should add a sixth goal to increase motivation
Goals only work if they are all started on the same day
Time and attention are finite, so running five starts in parallel diluted effort; sequencing one or two first would give each a real chance
Five goals failed, so goal-setting itself does not work for him

explanation: The constraint is not ambition but hours and attention. Choosing a lead goal for this season and parking the rest, with a review date, protects progress on something instead of thin progress on everything.
